I am a woman of 46 years here in Iringa, and this small plot of beans is only a corner of my land, just a bit bigger than my kitchen garden. I keep beans here because they feed my family and help the soil, and I plant them together with maize like my mother taught me. I cannot afford to buy chemical fertilizer for such a small bean plot — beans make their own goodness in the soil — but I will spread the manure from my goats and chickens. I will use the seeds I saved from last harvest, and my children and I will do the weeding ourselves; the rains here in Iringa are enough, so I do not need to carry water.
